title: Derandomization of Max-Cut via Conditional Expectations
description: Formalizes the method of conditional expectations for MaxCut: a deterministic greedy algorithm that processes vertices in order, always choosing the side that maximizes cut weight to placed vertices, achieving cut weight at least W/2.

meta.author: Erdős (1965), Sahni-Gonzalez (1976), formalized in Lean 4
originalContributions: greedyStep, greedyPartition: constructive greedy MaxCut algorithm in Lean 4
greedyContrib_ge_half: each greedy step cuts >= half the edge weight
conditional_expectation_method: abstract averaging argument for finite types

overview.historicalContext: The probabilistic method shows that a random partition of a graph cuts at least half the total edge weight in expectation. The method of conditional expectations (Spencer 1987, based on ideas from Erdős 1965 and Sahni-Gonzalez 1976) converts this into a deterministic algorithm: process vertices in order, and for each vertex choose the side that maintains the conditional expectation above W/2. For MaxCut, this simplifies to a greedy algorithm: put each vertex on the side opposite to where it has more edge weight.
overview.problemStatement: Constructively prove that for any weighted graph, there exists a partition cutting at least half the total edge weight (the exists_good_partition axiom from RandomizedMaxcutOQ02.lean).
overview.proofStrategy: Define a greedy algorithm that processes vertices in order. For each vertex k with the current partition S of vertices 0..k-1, the vertex is placed in S if the weight to S-complement exceeds the weight to S (maximizing cut contribution). The key inequality max(a,b) >= (a+b)/2 shows each vertex contributes at least half its total edge weight to already-placed vertices. Summing gives total cut >= W/2.
keyInsights: The greedy algorithm is remarkably simple: for each vertex, place it opposite to where it has more connections. No SDP, no randomness, no rounding.
The max_ge_avg inequality is the mathematical core: max(a,b) >= (a+b)/2 captures why the greedy choice always does at least as well as random.
The conditional_expectation_method theorem is the abstract principle: if the average over a finite type is >= c, some element achieves >= c. This is the probabilistic method in its simplest form.
The 1/2-approximation ratio is tight: a complete bipartite graph K_{n,n} with balanced partition already achieves exactly W/2.

sections.title: Part I: The Greedy Partition
sections.summary: Defines greedyStep (one vertex placement) and greedyPartition (fold over all vertices). The greedy rule: put vertex k opposite to where it has more edge weight.
sections.mathContext: For vertex $k$ with partition $S$ of $\{0, \ldots, k-1\}$: if $\sum_{j \in S^c} w(k,j) \geq \sum_{j \in S} w(k,j)$, put $k$ in $S$; otherwise in $S^c$.

sections.title: Part II: Cut Weight Lower Bound
sections.summary: max_ge_avg: the key inequality. greedyContrib_ge_half: each vertex contributes at least half its edge weight to already-placed vertices.
sections.mathContext: $\max(a,b) \geq (a+b)/2$ for $a, b \geq 0$. Applied to each vertex's edge weights to $S$ and $S^c$.

sections.title: Part III: Deterministic Existence
sections.summary: exists_good_partition': the main theorem showing the greedy partition achieves >= W/2. Has 1 sorry for the inductive fold assembly.

sections.title: Part V: Abstract Conditional Expectations
sections.summary: conditional_expectation_method: if the average of f over a finite type is >= c, some element achieves >= c. Proved by contradiction using sum comparison.
sections.mathContext: If $\frac{1}{|A|} \sum_{a \in A} f(a) \geq c$, then $\exists a \in A$ with $f(a) \geq c$. This is the core of the probabilistic method.

conclusion.summary: Formalizes the method of conditional expectations for MaxCut derandomization. Defines a constructive greedy algorithm, proves the key inequality max(a,b)>=(a+b)/2, and proves the abstract conditional expectations principle. 1 sorry remains for the inductive fold assembly. 0 axioms, 5 theorems, 170 lines.
conclusion.implications: The method of conditional expectations is one of the most important derandomization techniques in combinatorics and algorithms. This formalization demonstrates the pattern: probabilistic existence -> greedy algorithm -> deterministic guarantee. The same technique applies to MAX-SAT (Johnson 1974), coloring, and many other optimization problems.
openQuestions: Can the Goemans-Williamson SDP relaxation (0.878-approximation) be formalized in Lean 4?
Can the method of conditional expectations be generalized to a reusable Lean 4 tactic or framework?
